title: NAWA Holding
tagline: Corporate web presence for a holding company, rebuilt through three iterations to reach a production-grade result.
overview: NAWA Holding's site went through three distinct builds — an early Vite/React prototype, a Next.js iteration to test structure, and a final production version with polished motion using GSAP and Lenis smooth scrolling.
problem: The client needed a corporate site that felt as established as the holding company itself, but early iterations felt generic and lacked the smoothness expected from a modern corporate brand.
solution: Rather than patch the first version, I rebuilt the site on Next.js with GSAP-driven scroll animations and Lenis for smooth scrolling, treating the earlier builds as throwaway prototypes to learn from.
architecture: Next.js app router site with GSAP ScrollTrigger animations tied to section reveals, Lenis for inertia-based smooth scrolling, and a component structure carried over conceptually (but not literally) from the earlier prototypes.
features: Scroll-driven section reveals using GSAP ScrollTrigger
Structured content sections for company divisions and values
challenges: Recognizing early that the first two iterations weren't worth incrementally fixing, and rebuilding instead
Tuning GSAP animations so they felt premium without becoming distracting on a corporate site
lessonsLearned: Sometimes the fastest path to a good result is rebuilding from a clean slate rather than patching a fundamentally weak structure
Smooth scroll libraries like Lenis need careful tuning on lower-end devices to avoid feeling sluggish
futureImprovements: CMS integration so content updates don't require a redeploy
results: Production site reflecting the polish expected of an established holding company
